content:
The image shows soybean seeds held in a hand. Key observations:
- Seeds are yellow/cream colored (normal soybean background)
- Many seeds show purple to dark violet blotches/spots, ranging from small specks to covering a large portion of the seed surface
- The discoloration appears concentrated near and around the hilum area
- Some seeds are unaffected (pure yellow), showing the contrast clearly
- No shriveling or cracking visible — seeds appear plump

This pattern — pink to purple seed discoloration, especially extending from the hilum area — is the hallmark of **Purple_Seed_Stain** (caused by *Cercospora kikuchii*). The description matches exactly: "pink to purple spots ranging from specks to large blotches covering the entire surface, with discoloration extending from the seed hilum."

Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus can also cause seed coat mottling (brown/black), but that tends to be brown/black mottling, not purple. Phomopsis causes cracked, shriveled, gray-moldy seeds — not the case here.
